item.title: CERN congratulates Nobel Prize winner Francis Halzen
item.description: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics has been awarded to Francis Halzen for his contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory, which discovered high-energy neutrinos coming from far beyond our Solar System. This work is paving the way for a new generation of observatories to exploit neutrinos as a unique messenger of extreme environments in the […]

CERN launches the Grand Prix Resonance, a special edition of the annual Resonance residency programme
item.description: Arts at CERN, the City of Geneva and the Republic and Canton of Geneva are pleased to announce the launch of the Grand Prix Resonance, the third year of the Resonance residency programme. Resonance is a fully funded two-month residency at CERN for artists based in Geneva exploring the connections between art, science and technology. The programme, which started […]

item.title: Beam tests boost progress on detector technologies for the Future Circular Collider
item.description: The proposed Future Circular Collider (FCC) at CERN would put the Universe under a microscope like never before. By colliding electrons and positrons at four points around a 91 km ring, it would enable scientists to pin down the properties of the Higgs boson and other fundamental particles with a precision beyond the reach of […]

item.title: CERN entrepreneurship highlighted in global innovation report
item.description: The Global Innovation Index (GII) looks at innovation across 139 economies using 79 indicators and asks how economies can turn scientific breakthroughs into scalable ventures. CERN contributed to the latest edition of the report, launched on 29 September and entitled Powering entrepreneurs at the frontier of science, with a paper on CERN Venture Connect (CVC), […]

item.title: 中微子第五次获诺奖，2030年前能否揭开质量顺序之谜？
item.description: 中微子探测天文台冰立方首席科学家弗朗西斯·哈尔岑（Francis Halzen）获得2026年诺贝尔物理学奖，这是中微子相关研究第五次获得诺贝尔奖的青睐。

item.title: “冰立方”中微子天文台科学家获得2026年物理诺奖
item.description: 2026年诺贝尔物理学奖得主弗朗西斯·哈尔岑（Francis Halzen）推动了人类把南极洲下面一立方公里的冰，变成了一台“望远镜”。

item.title: New research shows a neutrino laser is impossible
item.description: Due to physical and fundamental limitations, an earlier proposal for producing laserlike beams of neutrinos cannot be achieved, scientists report.

item.title: On the hunt for dark matter
item.description: From Broadway to MIT’s Laboratory for Nuclear Science, PhD student Jessica Fry doesn’t do anything halfway. Now she’s hunting for the universe’s most elusive particle.

item.title: Lost quantum traces could reveal dark matter at the Large Hadron Collider
item.description: Particle collisions are inherently quantum, but much of that character is lost when we turn them into classical data. Sarah Alam Malik explores whether preserving more of it could help us spot signs of dark matter and other new physics

item.title: Physicists are scrambling to make sense of possible dark matter signal
item.description: Following the possible recent detection of a dark matter particle, researchers have already come up with a veritable cornucopia of possible models for what sort of particle it might have been

item.title: How an MIT graduate student helped a team of young scientists test their experiment at CERN
item.description: Physics PhD student Manu Srivastava helped high school students in India develop a test that could contribute to one of the world’s largest neutrino experiments.
